title: At-Takwir: the sun wrapped
hook: when the sun is folded up and the stars fall (81:1–2)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Infitar, the sky cleaves, and a body created, fashioned and balanced. Your line was shaped in proportion.

The most reliable thing you know isn't a person or a job. It's something that has never once let you down. For almost everyone, it's the sun. It came up this morning. It came up the day you were born, and the day your grandparents were born. Every plan anyone has ever made assumes it. Now a voice begins: when the sun is folded up. The surah just before Al-Infitar starts right there, with the one thing nobody doubts, and keeps going, a long list of whens. Today: At-Takwir, the sun wrapped.
screen: `THE MOST RELIABLE THING YOU KNOW.` → `WHEN THE SUN IS FOLDED UP.` → `AT-TAKWIR, THE SUN WRAPPED.`

segments.voice: Surah eighty-one begins, in Pickthall's words: When the sun is overthrown, And when the stars fall. The Arabic verb is kuwwirat, from takwir, a picture from everyday clothing. Kawwara is what you do with a turban: wind the cloth around and around until it's wrapped up. So the sun, which spreads its light across everything, is wound up like cloth and put away. Then the list rolls on. The stars fall and dim. The mountains are moved. The camels ten months pregnant, the most precious thing a family in Arabia could own, are left untended, because nobody is thinking about wealth anymore. The wild animals are gathered. The seas are set alight. Twelve whens in all, and after them, one line: then a soul will know what it has brought. A hadith in Tirmidhi says that whoever wants to see the Day of Resurrection as if with their own eyes should read this surah, and Al-Infitar, and Al-Inshiqaq, the three just walked through. Another hadith in Tirmidhi reports that when Abu Bakr told the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ his hair had turned gray, he named a few surahs that had done it, and this was one. So why start with the sun? Because if even the sun can be wrapped and put away, so can everything. Every tower, every fortune, every plan. The Qur'an says it elsewhere plainly: everyone upon the earth will pass away, and the face of your Lord remains. That isn't meant to make life feel pointless. It tells you where the one thing that lasts is.
screen: `KUWWIRAT — WOUND UP LIKE A TURBAN.` · `THE PRECIOUS CAMELS, LEFT UNTENDED.` · `TWELVE WHENS, THEN ONE SOUL.` · `IF EVEN THE SUN, THEN EVERYTHING.` · then, large: `EVERYTHING ENDS BUT HIM.`

segments.voice: Look at one thing near you that feels permanent, a wall, a table, a heavy old book: it was made, and one day it won't be here. Then bring to mind something heavier, a worry you've carried for months or a win you're proud of, and hold it lightly, the way you'd hold cloth you're about to fold and put away. Notice what's still here: your breath, this moment, and the One Muslims say remains.
At-Takwir. The wrapping up, the sun wound like a turban, and the name of Surah eighty-one. Today's word.
Your line: everything ends but him. If the sun can be wrapped, a worry or a win can sit a little lighter. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Muslims read At-Takwir together with Al-Infitar and Al-Inshiqaq as a picture of the Day of Resurrection, following a hadith that recommends them for that purpose; its opening is among the most widely memorized passages of the Qur'an.

fork.setup: At-Takwir lists the signs of the end. what happens to the camels ten months pregnant, the most precious thing a family owned?
options: they are sold at a high price
fork.reveal: they are abandoned (81:4). on that day, even the most valuable possession is forgotten.

original.note: Arabic: "is wound up," from k-w-r, to wind a turban; the sun is wrapped and put away (81:1).

trapdoor: what you thought: a surah about the end of the world.
what it means: twelve whens, beginning with the sun wound up like cloth, and then one soul knowing what it brought.

what a scholar hears: kawwara al-'imama, to wind a turban; Tirmidhi 3333 on seeing the Day in 81, 82 and 84; Tirmidhi 3297 on the surahs that grayed the Prophet's hair; 55:26–27 on everything passing but the face of your Lord.
recall: the constellations, the towers of the sky
the night visitor, the piercing star
